title: Farabbi2020: Motor-Imagery EEG dataset during robot-arm control
description: Motor-imagery EEG recorded from 12 healthy, BCI-naive participants performing cued left- versus right-hand imagery to control a Baxter robot arm reaching toward objects. Each participant completed three sessions with first-person and third-person visual feedback conditions, giving 480 trials per subject. Data were recorded with a 32-channel LiveAmp system at 250 Hz and re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 32-channel Brain Products LiveAmp and actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes (10-20 montage) at 250 Hz. Each session had four motor-imagery runs (first-person training/online, third-person training/online) of 20 left and 20 right trials, plus a resting-state recording. Each trial had a 2 s baseline followed by 4 s of imagery, with visual feedback from the robot arm.
